0.reason: the inline release covers the common case; the 30 s release tick re-derives waits and reaches the rest; unifying _release_waiters with advance_waiting_requests is follow-up work

findings.text: non-blocking: _release_waiters repeats the candidate scan and the resolve/move bookkeeping that advance_waiting_requests already owns at queue_admission.py:2561, and unlike that owner it never calls _rederive_waits, so a request whose waits a plan edit rewrote after it queued is not among the inline release's candidates; the 30 s tick still reaches it, but the inline route covers less than "every mover uses one function" implies.

non-blocking: the inline release derives readiness from the plan, and promotion writes no section_declarations itself, so it releases nothing unless the landing beat has already recorded the section as done at queue_landing.py:360; the service's ordering (land_once before admit_once, queue_admission.py:3822) makes that true today, but the docstring's "has now landed" claims more than the call can see, leaving a hand-promoted run silently releasing nobody.
non-blocking: _json_line is defined and never called, and import json at line 15 exists only for it; dead code in a new test file suggests a JSON-shape assertion is made somewhere when none is.

item_verdicts.diff: read all three commits against c9aab06ac87 — 13b347150a adds _resolve_and_move, _release_waiters, _release_tick and the promotion/discard callers, 8337f6ebbf is formatting only, and 5558b4e7d5 adds the evidence fragment; reckon/crew/dispatch.py:274 replaces its inline resolve-then-move idiom with one call, so the duplicated idiom is retired rather than copied.
item_verdicts.done_when: read the node's FENCE — EVIDENCE measure against tests/test_a_landed_section_releases_its_waiters.py; every named arm is present — the promotion release with a neighbouring section left waiting at lines 119-140, the tick release and its pacing at 143-167, the raising release at 170-191, the patched count of the shared function at 194-213, and the discard arm at 232-246 — and I re-ran the gate at the reviewed head in a scratch extraction, which printed "6 passed", EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is "release a landed section's waiting requests without an admission pass"; reckon/crew/promotion.py:684 calls _release_waiters_of_the_landed_section from complete(), which hands the plan#section ref to queue_admission._release_waiters at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2403 and moves a waiting request to queued, while reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2486 adds the service's own 30 s release tick, so a release no longer waits behind a launch or landing pass.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the gate at "6 passed" EXIT=0, the negative control at "1 failed" EXIT=1 with the first arm red, the importer arms at 62 passed at base and 62 passed at head, and it states the queue_landing.py boundary under evidence_inputs instead of claiming the declaration write.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's six declared paths; the diff against c9aab06ac87 changes exactly reckon/crew/queue_admission.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/crew/promotion.py, tests/test_a_landed_section_releases_its_waiters.py and the always-permitted evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop/a-landed-section-releases-its-waiters.html, and nothing outside them.

justifications.durability: the recorded negative control removes the inline release call from reckon/crew/promotion.py:684 and the first arm reddens at tests/test_a_landed_section_releases_its_waiters.py:137, and each remaining arm names a condition under which it fails (the tick not running at line 158, a raising release propagating at line 185, dispatch bypassing the shared function at line 203); the clock assertion at line 163 compares the value handed to _release_tick against what the store kept, which is falsifiable only through the skipped tick at line 161.
justifications.evidence: the gate log records "6 passed" EXIT=0 and I re-ran the same file against a git-archive extraction of 5558b4e7d5, which printed "6 passed" EXIT=0, so the measure holds at the reviewed head and not only on the worker's uncommitted tree.
justifications.fit: the new helpers are private and sit beside resolve_waits at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2345-2500, the comments describe latency and pacing rather than naming any plan, section or ticket, and the one public addition RELEASE_TICK_SECONDS at queue_admission.py:2479 is a module constant, not a callable definition.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/promotion.py:684 and reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2486 give the release both an inline route on landing and its own 30 s tick, so a landed ref reaches queued without an admission pass; the inline route's reach is narrowed by the promotion not writing the plan declaration itself (see the finding at promotion.py:684).
justifications.reuse: _resolve_and_move at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2345 wraps the existing resolve_waits and retires the copy in reckon/crew/dispatch.py:274, but _release_waiters at queue_admission.py:2403 re-walks the candidate scan that advance_waiting_requests already owns at queue_admission.py:2561 instead of extending it, and no owner for a paced tick exists anywhere in reckon/crew (the search found only this module's _RELEASE_TICK_LAST).
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat c9aab06ac87 5558b4e7d5 names five files, all inside the manifest's declared write paths, and the two pre-existing ruff findings at reckon/crew/promotion.py:1706 are present unchanged at the base revision (1666 there), so the commit adds no lint delta.
